claims.title: Covalent peptoid handover: intended bonds, false progression and spent-carrier destruction

quoted_fields.interface: Sar-initiated alpha-peptoid with20ordered additions, free N terminus and terminal carboxylic acid; DNA is a disposable recognition carrier rather than product backbone. Sixteen same-composition N2E6B6A6 programs have equal parent mass. Intended aminoacyl-thioester handover, hydrolytic dead acid, carrier-only exchange, recapture/duplicate additions, packet dimers/cycles, positional addresses, origin protection, carrier clearance and total initiated-product accounting are distinct operations.
quoted_fields.failure: Covalent ownership change is not a perfect intended-residue detector. Spent-thiol destruction and bound-DNA clearance have different timescales, and do not remove packet dimers, cyclization, damaged side groups or background insertions. Positive-case equal outputs assume equal rates/no sequence inhibition. Slow/no-collapse failure magnitudes omit escaped address-resolved thiol pools; higher oligomer waste lacks a constructed selective operation. Molecular consumables are replaced, not the same register renewed. ODE hidden labels do not supply assays or accepted-library probability. Full physical, economic, turnover, optical and large-library targets remain open.
